_doc: Rules of graph.extract.xlang (the cross-language edges). lit: a string literal that spells a repo-relative path (re, min and max length, and it must hold a '/' or end in an extension): ref kind lit, N edge to the file in graph.link. calls: per language FAMILY (langs.json family; c and c++ share cpp, javascript/typescript/tsx share js), a call whose callee text (as written, `new ` dropped, whitespace removed) matches re is read by role: exec = the leading run of string literals of the argument list is a command (join argv: one literal per argument, `Popen([a, b])`; join line: the literals are one command line, `Process.Start(file, args)`; a single literal is always a command line) read by graph.roots.command_targets (interpreters, launchers, builtins of frameworks.json), the program or script it names is an exec ref (T edge); env.r / env.w = the first literal (after skip arguments) names an environment variable that is read / written (`X=v` of putenv: the part before '='), cfg.r / cfg.w the same for a configuration key (System.getProperty, viper): refs of kind env named r:NAME / w:NAME and r:cfg:NAME / w:cfg:NAME. skip = leading arguments that are no literal (exec.CommandContext(ctx, ..), os.spawnv(mode, ..)). env_objects: the object whose member or subscript is an environment variable (process.env.X, os.environ["X"]). ffi_load (python): a call whose result is a handle of a native library (ctypes.CDLL, cffi dlopen); a member read of the handle is the native symbol (ref kind ffi). ffi_decl: a declaration that binds a native symbol: re must match the declaration text, entry (optional) is a group 1 regex of the symbol name in it, else the declared name; jni = the symbol is the JNI mangled Java_<package>_<class>_<method> of the package of the file and the class around the method. cmd: the family reads whole command lines (shell: every command node is a command line for graph.roots.command_targets). env_ambient: names every process has or every tool sets (HOME, PATH ...): no link. env_max_writers: a name that more places than this write is ambient too, over-wide is no information (graph.xlink). ffi_groups: the language groups (link groups or families) whose top-level functions a native import can reach (graph.link): a ref of kind ffi goes to the top-level defs of that name in them, T when there is one candidate, else N. schema: the references of the schema languages (sql, proto, graphql: graph.extract.schema defines their objects). A family with `schema_sql` reads every string literal that is a DML statement (sql.verb) for the tables it names (refs of kind schema, name `sql:<table>`; a name built at run time is a glob, `sql:audit_*`, `sql:*`). A statement written over several literals is one text: python `"SELECT a " + "FROM b"` and f-strings by `ast`; the tree-sitter families by `concat` = {node type: operator} of the node that joins operands (binary_expression + of java, js, go, c#; additive_expression + of kotlin, whose operator is no field; concatenated_string of c / c++, no operator): the literals are the text, any other operand a `{}` hole (`"SELECT * FROM " + t` names every table), a leading hole is dropped; a literal that is a part of such a chain is read only through it. A literal that starts with a clause (sql.clause: FROM, LEFT JOIN, the part a StringBuilder appends) names its tables too. The `schema.<group>` call role names a schema object by the first string literal of a call (graphql-java dataFetcher). schema.groups = the language groups of the schema files (fold = identifiers are case-insensitive, parent = a name that no object has falls back to its owner: `Book.author` to the type Book). schema.sql: verb = the start of a literal that is a statement, clause = the start of a literal that is the part of one (a clause that names a table), dml = the keywords that are followed by a table name (a FROM list too), ddl = more of them in a schema file, call = keywords followed by a routine name, stop = the words that end a FROM list, min / max = the length of a literal that is read, fold_max the length of a statement written over several operands (a long query is not a prose string). schema.proto: stubs = the names the generated code of a service, a message and a file has (`{n}` the name, `{f}` the file stem, `{F}` its CamelCase): `service` and `file_services` give the service(s), `file` the file itself. schema.graphql: roots = the root operation types (their fields are objects; a type that a `schema { query: X }` block names is one too), builtin = the scalars of the language, resolvers = the class names whose members are the resolvers of the fields of the root types (group 1 = the operation).
name: ^[A-Za-z_][\w.-]*$
